 Election results: Derek Tran, Chuong Vo face off in 45th Congressional District race 
 Tran, a Democrat seeking a second term in Congress, faces Republican challenger Vo, a former mayor of Cerritos.

 Derek Tran (left) and Chuong Vo are running for California’s 45th Congressional District in 2026. (Photos courtesy of the Tran and Vo campaigns)
 By Charlie Borla | cborla@scng.com PUBLISHED: November 3, 2026 at 8:43 PM PST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 Rep. Derek Tran , D-Orange, jumped out to an initial large lead against Republican Chuong Vo Tuesday night, according to early returns released by the California secretary of state’s office.
 Read more: Derek Tran and Chuong Vo look to their families when it comes to immigration policy in the race for California’s 45th Congressional District 
 The 45th Congressional District includes Cerritos in L.A. County, as well as Buena Park, Cypress, Fountain Valley, Garden Grove and Westminster in Orange County.
 Tran is finishing up his first term in Congress, where he represents a district that includes Orange County’s Little Saigon, home to the largest Vietnamese population outside of that country.
 A Republican, Vo is a former police officer who served for nearly three decades.
 Both candidates are children of Vietnamese refugees and have pointed to their families’ experiences when talking about immigration policy.
 Tran’s father,  like many others , fled Vietnam by boat after the fall of Saigon, but the boat capsized, killing his wife and children. His father would remarry, and the two would successfully leave Vietnam and settle in the U.S. Tran was born and raised in Los Angeles County, according to his House bio .
 Vo came to the U.S. from Vietnam as a refugee with his parents . On his campaign website , Vo noted that “like so many immigrant families, I’m grateful to a country that gave my family a chance, and I want to keep that promise alive for the next generation.”
 Democrats account for 38.77% (175,995 people) of registered voters in the district, according to the latest statistics from the California secretary of state’s office. Republicans, meanwhile, account for 30.08% (136,536), and no party preference 25.29% (114,816).
